checkpoint_review: I have re-evaluated the 'Eyes' checkpoint. While thunder snakes (Carphophis amoenus) do have minute eyes, they are typically visible as dark spots beneath the head scales upon close inspection. In this image, the head region is indeed smooth and lacks any discernible eye structure, even at high zoom. This confirms my initial finding of a missing anatomical feature. The Router's verdict of 'Checked' was incorrect; it likely assumed presence based on class priors rather than visual evidence. All other checkpoints remain valid. The ventral surface is correctly N/A. The tail end is blunt and consistent. Body shape, color, and scale gloss are accurate.
authenticity_review: My initial authenticity score of 3.85 may have been slightly harsh given the overall high quality. The missing eye is a subtle defect, not a gross structural failure like melting or extra limbs. The topology auditor confirmed excellent boundary integrity (0.987 confidence), and the perceptual auditor found only slight compression. Comparing to Reference 2 (alignment=4.29, auth=3.00) which shows multiple sharks with some blur/artifacts, this image is cleaner but has one specific anatomical flaw. Reference 3 (auth=4.00) is a bird with good detail. This snake image is closer to Ref 3 in cleanliness but penalized for the missing eye. A score of 4.0 seems more calibrated: it acknowledges the high fidelity of the rendered texture and form while accounting for the biological inaccuracy. I will adjust authenticity up slightly from 3.85 to 4.0 to better align with the reference anchors and avoid over-penalizing a single minor anatomical omission.
